card: GRB physics follow-up G3-10b/10c: is the mass-properties payload an inertia tensor?

first_fail.byte_layout: +0x2c..+0x2f is 4 bytes; a symmetric tensor needs 24 (six values) or 36 (nine values)

verdict.statement: the payload fails the four-part oracle: best layout i16_grouped_diag passes 27 of 54 bodies at 25% per-moment tolerance (median normalised error 0.252174, 40 pass at 50%)

unknowns: the scale that turns the quantised lanes into SI moments: no project decoder reads it, so only the shape of the moments is testable (all four oracle parts are scale-free). Candidate home: the fourth lane of each group (+0x16 11008..12544 and +0x1e 10368..13696), which stays in a narrow band in all 56 blocks and looks like an exponent or scale marker, but nothing in this tree documents it.

whether the third int16x4 group (+0x20..+0x27) is the three products or a principal axis: its triple norm is 1.3638..1.7321 in Q15, neither 1.0 (an axis) nor 0 (products near a principal frame), and two of its lanes are x-odd, which both readings allow.
whether the f32 at +0x2c is a volume, a density or an unused slot: it is 0 in 38 of 56 blocks and 0.0019..0.165 in the rest, with no monotone relation to the mass checked here.
the sign convention of the x-odd lanes (row vs column, right- vs left-handed). The mirror mask fixes *which* lanes are x-odd, not the handedness.

why box agreement fails: the hull is not a box (thin panels, curved doors), so the reference tensor itself is a model. A hull-exact tensor (tetrahedral decomposition of the polytope) would separate an encoding error from a reference-model error.
